anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have their GND1 and GND2 pins connected to the same common GND net.
anomalies.expected: An isolated CAN transceiver should keep GND1 (logic side) and GND2 (CAN side) as separate ground domains so the galvanic isolation is preserved, as the specification describes isolated CAN buses.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)
Interface_CAN_LIN:ISO1050DUB | Isolated CAN Transceiver, SOP-8 | pins: ... 4=GND1(power_in) 5=GND2(power_in)

anomalies.impact: The CAN isolation barrier is defeated, so the buses are not isolated from the logic ground and may suffer ground loops or reduced safety/robustness.

anomalies.observed: The net /LED_3.3V_POWER_SW connects only the anodes of LEDs D4, D14, and D23; it has no connection to +3V3 or any other supply/driver.
anomalies.expected: These LED anodes should be tied to a 3.3V power net, or to a switched 3.3V supply, so the LEDs can be driven by their cathode-side signals.

evidence.quote: D4 | LED_GREEN | LED_SMD:LED_0805_2012Metric | Device:LED | Light emitting diode

anomalies.impact: The Ethernet/link and PI activity LEDs connected to this net will not illuminate because their supply node is floating.

parsed.summary: The design files contain connectivity anomalies: the isolated CAN transceiver grounds are shorted together, defeating the specified CAN isolation, and a LED power net is left floating. These deviations would make the board behave differently from the intended isolated-CAN, status-LED design.
